title: High-Performance Data Pipeline Optimization
business: Data analytics firms processing massive telemetry streams.
problem: High memory overhead and slow iteration speeds when filtering large datasets using traditional object-oriented patterns.
solution: Utilizing D's native compilation and ranges to create zero-allocation, lazy-evaluated data pipelines that process telemetry in-place.
steps: Define a struct representing the telemetry data packet.
Implement the range interface (front, popFront, empty) on a wrapper struct to encapsulate the data source.
Apply template metaprogramming to create generic filtering functions that accept any range type.
Use the compiler's native ability to inline these range operations, eliminating function call overhead.
Verify memory footprint using static analysis to ensure no heap allocations occur during iteration.
outcome: Significant reduction in runtime memory pressure and improved throughput for stream processing tasks.
limitation: Template bloat can increase binary size and compile times; check this by monitoring object file sizes during iterative builds.

questions.question: In High-Performance Data Pipeline Optimization, how does the technology address the problem of high memory overhead?
options: By utilizing D's native compilation and ranges to create zero-allocation, lazy-evaluated data pipelines.
By replacing all structs with classes to enable better garbage collection.
By using a virtual machine to interpret data streams at runtime.
By offloading all filtering logic to an external C++ library.
questions.explanation: The solution explicitly states that D's ranges allow for zero-allocation pipelines, which directly addresses the memory overhead problem.
